takeaway: A U-shaped Transformer restores a degraded image; its blocks replace spatial attention with channel attention (MDTA) and a gated feed-forward (GDFN).
problem: Self-attention over pixels grows quadratically with image size, which is impractical for high-resolution restoration.

contributions.name: Multi-Dconv Head Transposed Attention (MDTA)
contributions.solves: attention cost at high resolution (attends across channels)
contributions.shown_by: orange Transformer-block tint, expanded in panel (a)

mechanism.explains: channel attention: Q, K, V from 1×1 + depth-wise convs, a C×C attention map instead of HW×HW
the gate: GELU on one depth-wise branch multiplies the other

depth.why: the 2-minute mechanism (attention across channels); drawn beside the U
the gated feed-forward the text pairs with MDTA in the same block

concepts.name: U-shape with two detail panels
concepts.takes: U layout, input/output images at the top corners, block detail beside the U

concepts.name: linear pipeline + one panel
concepts.takes: flat stage row with the new block expanded below

why: the paper's encoder–decoder is symmetric with skips; two contributions need two panels
highlight: orange tint on the Transformer block and both panels; reused levels in blue

data_visuals.what: degraded input (restored output uses the same frame)
data_visuals.path: demo/degraded/portrait.jpg (the Restormer repository's demo image, cropped to the subject)

omitted_details.what: progressive training on growing patch sizes
omitted_details.reason: a training schedule, not the architecture

core.why: the contribution is inside the repeated block: MDTA and GDFN only read when the block is opened beside the U

relations.form: a U laid sideways: down the encoder levels on the left, up the decoder on the right, left to right overall
detail panels below the U, tied to the block by the proposed tint

channels.colour: role and operator kind: proposed modules orange, reused levels blue, 1×1 / depth-wise convolutions and layer norm their own tones (color_semantics)
channels.shape: feature maps as stacks sized by resolution

structure.budget: the U is compact (one stack per level); half the height goes to the two detail panels, because the contribution lives there

layout.takes: the U: encoder levels down the left, decoder levels up the right, skips across at each level; detail panels below
layout.why: one network trained end to end: no streams or stages to separate
